diagnosis.source: P19 full-resume and identical-input Q-partition probes
diagnosis.mechanism: Q128-vs-Q32 attention differs with identical rotated queries and unchanged K/V cache/page table, while Q32 full and offset-slice attention are bitwise equal. The first full-layer non-exact capture for offset32/64 was finish.attention_input, before o_proj/CCL.
diagnosis.interpretation: Q partitioning explains the observed local discrepancy, and forcing Q32 everywhere passes the unchanged full-model resume gate. This does not prove a hardware defect or explain the historical origin beyond the measured causal behavior.

negative_controls.note: The two last-token cases do not run the 64-position negative controls.

precision_policy.scope: Only the diagnostic runner overrode the constructed geometry to Q32; policy JSON was unchanged.

production_change.behavior: Select prefill_q=32 when the model's SDPA compute fidelity is HiFi4; otherwise preserve the previous BF16-global=64 and default=128 geometry. The existing nonaligned-start Q32 arm and K32 literal remain unchanged.
production_change.head_bfp8_hifi2: Keeps its existing Q128 geometry because its SDPA fidelity is HiFi2 and its KV cache is BFP8.
production_change.not_yet_validated: Fresh-path natural accuracy, qualitative outputs, fixed108 precision regression, and performance for the changed HiFi4 Q32 configuration. Root owns those follow-up gates.

deferred_alternative.reason: Padded Q128 would require a phase-aligned expanded sliding page-table base and aligned chunk_start_idx. Native SDPA rejects scalar offsets not divisible by both Q and K chunks; the optional tensor-offset trace path additionally needs a warmed aligned offset/table input. The already-passing Q32 path is simpler but requires fresh-path acceptance reruns.
